datasets.title: Geodata of Damage Assesment in Bouar, Nana Membere Province, Central African republic
datasets.description: This map illustrates locations of destroyed structures in the Bouar area of Central African Republic. Using a satellite image acquired 04 March 2014 by the WorldView-2 satellite, UNOSAT reviewed the town of Bouar and surrounding areas to locate signs of destroyed structures. A total of 506 destroyed structures were identified as of 4 March 2014, and a previous UNOSAT analysis using an image from 22 January 2014 indicated that 366 of the structures were destroyed as of that date. Some of the visible destruction is possibly the result of burning given the blackened structural remains visible in the imagery. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR / UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assesment-in-bouar-nana-membere-province-central-african-re-march-14-2014]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts reviewed WorldView-2 satellite imagery acquired on 4 March 2014 and compared it with a previous image from 22 January 2014 to identify structural damage in Bouar, Central African Republic. Visual interpretation of satellite imagery detected 506 destroyed structures as of March 2014, with 366 confirmed destroyed as of January 2014, using change detection and damage signature analysis.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis (WorldView-2) comparing pre- and post-event conditions to identify destroyed structures through visual interpretation of damage signatures including burned remains.
